title: Exact inverse image preserves K-flat resolutions
statement: Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. There exists an additive functor $I:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(g^{-1}\mathcal O_S)$ whose objects and maps are the canonical module inverse images [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module]. This functor preserves finite limits and finite colimits. For every quasi-isomorphism $s:P^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] with $P^\bullet$ K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], the termwise map $I(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $I(P^\bullet)$ is K-flat over $g^{-1}\mathcal O_S$.

proof.text: The canonical inverse-image maps preserve identity, composition and addition since their underlying abelian-sheaf maps do. They therefore assemble to the additive functor I with the recorded objects and maps.

At t in T, the underlying abelian stalk of I(M) is naturally the stalk M at g(t). Exactness of sheaf sequences is checked on stalks, so I preserves finite limits and finite colimits. Its termwise functor preserves homology and hence quasi-isomorphisms.

Apply K-flat pullback preservation to (T,g^{-1} O_S) -> (S,O_S) with adjoint ring map the identity. Tensoring over g^{-1} O_S with that same ring is naturally the identity on modules and on complexes, so this pullback is I(P). Thus I(P) is K-flat. Combining this with the previous quasi-isomorphism clause proves resolution preservation.
